newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian GIMV confirms stock market listing plans.
newsitem.headline: Belgian GIMV confirms stock market listing plans.

text.p: Belgium's Flemish regional investment company GIMV is to go ahead with its plans to list on the Brussels Stock Exchange in June, its chairman said on Thursday.
"The decision was taken by the board on Tuesday and has been approved by the (Flemish) government. We are going ahead," Chairman Raynier van Outryve d'Ydewalle told Reuters.
Van Outryve said the listing would "probably take place in June" with the proviso that if the stock market were to crash between now and then it could be postponed.

As decided last year, the Flemish government - which owns 85 percent of GIMV will list "around 15 percent" of its holding. Fifteen percent of GIMV is already in private hands following a private placement in 1995.
Van Outryve said brokerage Petercam had been charged with providing a valuation of the company, preparing the prospectus and identifying lead managers for the issue.
"Petercam will not participate in the placing of the shares. We are keeping the two parts of the procedure separate," Van Outryve said.

GIMV's stock market listing has been in the pipeline for several years. Last year the plan hit a snag over what the company should do with its cash mountain -- due principally to the sale last year of interests in companies such as Plant Genetic Systems NV, Lernout & Hauspie and Innogenetics.
Van Outryve said, however, it had been decided the cash would stay with the GIMV.
"We are preparing a new mission statement about how we will spend our cash in the coming four or five years -- what GIMV's priorities are," he said.

GIMV's main interests include 33.5 percent of Belgian electronics firm Barco, around 10 percent of engineering company BMT and a small interest in specialist, Nasdaq-listed printing software firm Xeikon.
GIMV is also a shareholder in Europe's Easdaq growth stocks market.
